A larger interim payment adds to the return.
Paying more at the start lowers the return on the same ending value.

intuition: Log of the gross return: continuous compounding, and the implied price can never go negative.

intuition: Count the tail (alpha times n) and step one past it: 1,000 obs at 97% puts the VaR at the 31st worst loss.

forecast change in loans over the planning period (a demand for liquidity)

corruptions.latex: \text{Liquidity gap} = \text{Estimated change in loans} - \text{Estimated change in deposits}
corruptions.why: Reversed: liquidity rises as deposits increase and loans decrease, so a surplus (positive gap) means more deposits than loans.

corruptions.latex: \text{Liquidity gap} = \text{Estimated change in deposits} + \text{Estimated change in loans}
corruptions.why: Loans are a use of funds: a loan increase drains liquidity, so it is subtracted, not added.

sensitivities.why: Liquidity rises as deposits increase.
Liquidity declines when loans increase.

intuition: Deposits in, loans out: more deposit growth than loan growth is a surplus (positive gap), the reverse is a deficit.

name: Repo settlement amount (general form)
prompt: What does the borrower pay back to close a repo, allowing for accrued interest and a haircut?

variables.meaning: amount repaid at the repo's maturity (repurchase price)
market value of the collateral bond (the contract price), not its face value
accrued interest on the collateral bond
haircut applied to the collateral (decimal)
repo rate (decimal, annual)
repo term as a fraction of a year on an actual/360 basis (days/360)

corruptions.why: A haircut reduces the cash lent against the collateral, so it is (1 - haircut).
Omits accrued interest: one of the three recycled distractors, one per omitted input.
The contract price is the bond's market value, not its face ($11m, not $10m, in the notes' example).

sensitivities.why: More valuable collateral supports a larger loan to repay.
Accrued interest is part of the collateral's full value.
A bigger haircut means less cash lent, so less to repay.
A higher repo rate means more interest.
A longer term accrues more interest.

intuition: Cash lent = full collateral value less the haircut; grow it at the repo rate on actual/360 to get what comes back.

name: Failed-delivery penalty rate (post-2009)
prompt: Since 2009, what penalty rate applies to a failed Treasury delivery, given the fed funds rate?

variables.meaning: penalty rate on failed deliveries (%); the upper limit for the special spread since 2009
federal funds rate (%)

corruptions.why: The penalty moves against the fed funds rate: high rates, low penalty.
Reversed: the penalty is at its maximum of 3% when the fed funds rate is zero.
It is the greater of 3% minus FFR or zero; a min would make the penalty zero or negative.

sensitivities.why: Falls one-for-one as the fed funds rate rises, until it hits zero at FFR = 3%.

intuition: Failing costs you a day's interest anyway; the penalty tops that up to 3%, so it is biggest when rates are zero.

name: Financing value of a special: per 100 of cash
prompt: What is the financing value, per 100 of cash, of a bond expected to trade special for a number of days?

variables.meaning: financing advantage per 100 market value of the bond
horizon over which the bond is expected to keep trading special
GC rate minus special rate (decimal)

corruptions.why: Repo is actual/360; using 365 gives 0.0753 instead of 0.0764.
The advantage is the spread earned (GC minus special), not the whole GC rate.
The value accrues with time: days multiply the spread.

sensitivities.why: The longer the bond stays special, the more financing value.
A wider spread below GC means cheaper financing.

intuition: Interest saved: the special spread earned on 100 of cash for the days it stays special, actual/360.

name: Financing value of a special: per 100 face
prompt: How do you convert the financing value per 100 of cash into a value per 100 face amount of the bond?

variables.meaning: financing advantage per 100 face amount
financing advantage per 100 market value
the bond's market price per 100 face

corruptions.why: A bond priced above par ties up more than 100 of cash per 100 face, so scale up by price/100.
Dividing by DV01 is the next step (yield value in bp), not the face conversion.

sensitivities.why: Scales one-for-one.
A higher price means more cash financed per 100 face.

intuition: Per 100 face you finance Price, not 100, of cash; so scale by price/100 (7.6 cents becomes 7.7).

name: Financing value of a special: yield value in bp
prompt: How do you translate the financing value per 100 face into a yield value in basis points?

variables.meaning: financing advantage expressed in basis points of yield
financing advantage per 100 face amount
dollar value of a basis point per 100 face

corruptions.why: Dollar value divided by DV01 gives basis points; multiplying gives 0.0065, not a plausible magnitude.
Upside down: the dollar value is the numerator.

sensitivities.why: More dollar value is more basis points.
A more rate-sensitive bond needs fewer bp to be worth the same dollars.

intuition: Dollars divided by dollars-per-bp gives bp: 0.077 / 0.085 is about 0.9 bp.

name: Special spread
prompt: How is the special spread of a bond defined in terms of repo rates?

variables.meaning: GC rate minus special rate for that security and term; floored at 0, capped by the GC rate (and since 2009 by the penalty rate)
general collateral repo rate (the highest repo rate)
repo rate on the specific security (below GC)

corruptions.why: Specials trade BELOW GC, so the spread is GC minus special; reversing gives a negative number.
The spread is measured from the GC rate, which sits below the fed funds rate.

sensitivities.why: A higher GC rate widens the gap to the special rate.
A lower special rate (a scarcer bond) widens the spread.

intuition: How far below GC the bond's repo rate is pushed by demand to borrow it; FFR > GC > special.
